full_judgment:
The above numbered 2(two) revisions arise out of the same judgment and decree dated 13-2-2006, passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet, in Title Appeal No. 72 1994, reversing those dated 30-3-1994, passed by the Assistant Judge, Balaganj, Sylhet, in Title Suit No. 02 of 1984. 

 8. After hearing the parties the learned Assistant Judge by the judgment and decree dated 30-3-1995 dismissed the suit. 

 9. On appeal, the judgment and decree of the trial Court were reversed and set by the impugned judgment and decree dated 13-2-2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet, in Title Appeal No. 72 of 1995. 

 10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree 2(two) sets of defendants as petitioners preferred the above numbered 2(two) revisions and obtained the Rules. 

 11. In course of argument the petitioners of Civil Revision No. 3814 of 2006 filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil. Procedure to accept a kabala annexed to the that application as Annexure-A as additional evidence. Mr Md Ibrahim Mollah the learned Advocate appearing for them submits that they accrued right, title and interest in a part of the suit land by the said deed, regarding their such claim they made averments in their pleading but could not produce the document during the trial of the suit and hearing of the appeal. After preferring this revision they could manage a certified copy of the said deed and, as such, to adjudicate the dispute finally the said deed may be accepted as additional evidence, for that purpose the suit may be sent back on remand to the appellate Court after setting aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

 (a) the Court from whose decree the appeal is preferred has refused to admit evidence which ought to have been admitted, or (b) the appellate Court requires any document to be produced or any witness to be examined to enable it to pronounce judgment or for any other substantial cause, the Appellate Court may allow such evidence or document to be produced or witness to be examined. 

 15. On perusal of the application it appears to me that sub-rule 1 (a) is not applicable in the instant case, rather the provision in sub-rule 1(b) is applicable. This Court in the decisions cited above decided that the provision of accepting additional evidence in appellate Court is also applicable in the revisional forum but such acceptance should be allowed after the assigning reason as per sub-section 1(b). The instant suit was nothing but a suit for partition and in absence of any share of any defendant/s there is no reason to impleade him/her/ them. as defendant/s in the suit. On perusal of the judgment of the Courts below it appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit but the appellate Court decreed the suit giving no saham to the petitioners through as defendants of the suit they cannot be sahamless, but the question remained whether their share/s had been transferred or not, and such question about transfer could be decided by the Court below. Annexure-A to the application filed by the petitioners is apparently a deed of transfer executed in favour of Mazid Ullah who is the admitted predecessor of the application of the said application, and regarding Mazid Ullah apparently they made, averments in their pleadings. Comparing schedule appended to the said deed with that of the plaint it appears that the land described in the schedule appended to the said deed is not beyond the area of the land described in the schedule appended to the plaint and, as such, this deed deserve consideration by the Court as evidence. Accordingly I am inclined to allow the said application and to send back the suit to the appellate Court on remand for hearing afresh after considering the said deed as evidence of the suit. 

 16. In the result, both the Rules are hereby made absolute and the judgment and decree impugned in both the revisions are hereby set aside and the suit is hereby sent back on remand to the appellate Court for hearing afresh on consideration of the said deed as additional evidence, the parties will be at liberty to examine oral witness in support of against the said deed and they will be also at liberty to amend their respective pleading if necessary. However, the appellate Court is hereby directed to dispose up the appeal within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.
